title: Telemetry + cost attribution: tag quantized vs baseline execution for token-level reporting
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Problem
We need to ensure every request has consistent token-level cost + latency attribution that can differentiate baseline execution from quantized execution. This must work even when quantization is enabled per-route with canaries, and when we fall back to baseline due to incompatibility.

Why this matters
- Console dashboards (Optimize / route breakdown) need to show: (a) cost delta, (b) latency delta, and (c) adoption rate (% quantized) per route and per model.
- Billing hooks must not mis-attribute cost or double count when execution mode changes mid-rollout.
- SRE needs alerting segmentation to isolate regressions to a specific profile/version.

Requirements / Acceptance Criteria
1) Runtime emits a stable set of tags for every completion/embedding request:
   - execution_mode: baseline | quantized
   - quantization_profile_id: <string> (empty/"none" when baseline)
   - quantization_profile_version: <semver> (empty/"none" when baseline)
   - quantization_kernel_path: <string> (e.g., "awq.int4", "gptq.int4", "cutlass.int8", "baseline.fp16")
   - quantization_fallback_reason: <enum> (only present when requested quantization but executed baseline)
2) Tags propagate consistently to:
   - tracing spans (request root span + model execution span)
   - request metrics (latency histograms; error counters)
   - cost attribution pipeline (token accounting events)
3) Cost attribution events can be joined/grouped by route + execution_mode + profile_id/version.
4) If a request is routed to a quantized-capable worker but falls back, it must still be labeled baseline (and include fallback reason) to avoid inflating quantized adoption.
5) Console dashboards can slice route costs by execution_mode (baseline vs quantized) without custom ad-hoc parsing.

Implementation plan
- Add execution mode + profile metadata to request context at the point where runtime resolves the effective profile (post-policy evaluation, pre-kernel selection).
- Ensure fallback path overwrites mode to baseline and sets quantization_fallback_reason.
- Update token accounting emitter to include tags on every emission (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens).
- Add metric tags to:
  - request_latency_seconds{route, model, execution_mode, quantization_profile_id, quantization_profile_version}
  - request_tokens_total{route, model, token_type, execution_mode, quantization_profile_id, quantization_profile_version}
  - request_errors_total{route, model, status_code, execution_mode, quantization_profile_id, quantization_profile_version}
- Update the billing hook mapping to support "none" profile values without breaking existing aggregations.

Testing / Validation
- Unit tests: tagging logic for (a) baseline, (b) quantized, (c) fallback to baseline.
- Integration test: canary rollout 10% with mixed traffic; verify that adoption ~= 10% and not 0/100 due to sampling.
- Backfill check in staging: compare sum(tokens_total) by route vs existing totals (must match within 0.1%).
- Smoke test with long-context workload where we’ve seen fallback due to kernel constraints.

Out of scope
- Customer-facing API response fields (handled by SDK/types work).
- Dashboards themselves (tracked separately by Console team).

comments: 2025-01-14 (Logan Wright): Marking P0 because we cannot ship route-scoped quantization without reliable tagging. Optimize dashboards + billing attribution depend on this being correct during canaries + rollbacks.

2025-01-16 (Nadia Rahman): Proposed tag set looks good. One concern: do not use high-cardinality tags for kernel path if it can vary per request (e.g., per-seq-len). Suggest keep kernel_path limited to coarse enum values. If we need deeper kernel debugging, keep that in traces/logs only.

2025-01-17 (Mateo Alvarez): Runtime can provide a stable execution_mode + profile_id/version at resolution time. Kernel_path can be coarse ("baseline.fp16", "int8", "int4") as Nadia suggests. Fallback reason enum should include: INCOMPATIBLE_GPU, UNSUPPORTED_SEQ_LEN_BIN, PROFILE_NOT_FOUND, PROFILE_SIGNATURE_INVALID, RUNTIME_ERROR.

2025-01-21 (Cole Summers): Billing side: please ensure token accounting event schema change is backward compatible. If fields are absent, billing currently assumes baseline. Prefer explicit execution_mode field with default baseline and profile fields set to "none" to avoid NULL semantics in the pipeline.

2025-01-24 (Nadia Rahman): Implemented tagging in token accounting emitter + metrics. Using explicit values: execution_mode=(baseline|quantized) and quantization_profile_id/version=(none|<value>). Added fallback_reason only when policy requested quantization but mode==baseline.

2025-01-27 (Rafael Mendes): Canary validation request: we need to confirm that during canary % the tag distribution matches rollout decision per-route. Please add a staging runbook snippet: query request_tokens_total grouped by execution_mode and confirm 10% ± 2% for stable traffic.
2025-01-29 (Nadia Rahman): Opened PR for tags + propagation; added integration test that forces fallback by simulating unsupported GPU arch in runtime compat check. Link: pr_28833.

2025-02-03 (Logan Wright): Verified in staging: token totals match pre-change within 0.04% across top 20 routes. Adoption metric slices correctly for mixed canary traffic. Marking Done once PR merged and deployed to runtime-1.18.
